title: National platform becomes unavailable during a peak service window
context: A business-critical public-sector platform is down, multiple stakeholders are escalating, and technical evidence is incomplete.
steps: Establish incident command and protect service/user safety
Separate symptom containment from root-cause investigation
Create a single source of truth for stakeholders and decision rights
Restore minimum viable service before nonessential optimization
Run post-incident review with ownership, resilience and monitoring actions
tradeoffs: Central command vs. distributed technical ownership

title: ERP / enterprise application program is nine months late
context: Vendor, internal teams and business owners disagree on scope, dependencies and accountability.
steps: Re-baseline scope and critical outcomes
Map unresolved decisions and ownership gaps
Split recoverable work from structural blockers
Introduce milestone evidence and executive governance cadence
Renegotiate vendor commitments against measurable acceptance criteria
tradeoffs: Big-bang completion vs. staged value release

title: AI program is scaling without governance or trusted data access
context: Business demand is high, pilots are multiplying, but data quality, ownership, security and human oversight are inconsistent.
steps: Inventory use cases and classify risk
Define data access, ownership and lineage requirements
Establish responsible-AI decision rights and human oversight
Prioritize use cases with measurable value and manageable risk
Instrument monitoring, model/change controls and outcome review
metrics: time from pilot to controlled production

title: Critical technology capability is constrained by vendor lock-in
context: Costs are rising and switching is difficult because integrations, data and operational knowledge are concentrated with one supplier.
steps: Quantify technical, commercial and knowledge concentration
Identify contractual and architectural exit constraints
Separate data portability, interface portability and operational capability
Design phased optionality rather than a disruptive immediate exit
Embed knowledge-transfer and interoperability milestones into governance

title: Executives do not trust the enterprise data warehouse
context: Reports conflict, definitions differ across departments and decision-makers revert to spreadsheets.
steps: Identify high-value decisions and authoritative measures
Map conflicting definitions to data ownership
Introduce master/reference data and validation controls
Publish lineage and reconciliation evidence
Rebuild adoption around a small set of trusted executive products
tradeoffs: Speed of reporting vs. validation depth
